briefFidelity: FAIL — and this is the gate. The brief is titled FILIGREE and restates delicacy four separate times: 'delicate, fine and fragile', 'hairline linework', 'light enough that the work feels provisional — as though it could be disturbed', 'nothing heavy, nothing solid', and 'the contrast kept low so the lines read as thread rather than as structure'. Delivered on the majority of the twelve is a confident high-contrast emblem. Measured on the 256 sheet: the brightest carrier stroke is rgb(217,210,194) against a rgb(15,17,19) ground — roughly 13:1, essentially maximal contrast, where the brief asked for it to be kept low — and the median bright stroke run is 5-6px at 256, about 2.3% of the canvas, which is a medium confident line rather than a hairline. The tell is my own blind description: without having seen the brief I called these 'emblems', 'sigils', a 'seal', a 'technical schematic', named a bone 'carrier line' holding the silhouette, and wrote 'heavy alpha layering'. I did not reach for delicate, fine, fragile, thread, provisional or light once. The brief predicted exactly this failure mode by name — 'reads as structure' — and that is what a cold reader saw. Four or five tokens (9369, 10085, 10443, 10801, and the 512 single) do land the filigree register; the other seven, and specifically 9906, 9011, 10622 and 10264, read as stamped seals. Everything else in the brief is met: cool bone-and-pale-slate over dark ground is exact, the radial figure is exact, and 'no filled mass anywhere' is strictly true — every mark is a stroke.
seedVariation: PASS — correctly in the middle, neither extreme. On the 120px sheet the twelve separate into real classes: hexagonal carriers (9011, 9190, 10264, 10622, 10801, 10980), plain circles (9369, 9906, 10085), a rotated diamond (10443), and dense polygon-stars (9548, 9727). Interior density spans three dots inside a bare ring up to an edge-to-edge woven lattice, and roughly half carry orbiting satellites while half do not. Two tokens do converge — 9369 and 10085 are hard to separate at browse size — but that is a single collision, not a collection reading as one work. The brief's 'tokens differ in the symmetry of the figure and in how far its threads extend' is satisfied, though weighted heavily toward 6-fold: seven of twelve are hexagonal.
thumbnailSurvival: PASS, and ironically it survives partly for the wrong reason. At 120px the base polygon, the bright bone rim, the satellite arrangement and the density class all read cleanly, and the twelve remain twelve. What is lost is the interior geometry as discrete members — the dense tokens collapse to woven texture and the central clusters to a smudge. But the reason the silhouette holds so firmly is the 13:1 carrier stroke, i.e. the same property that breaks the brief. A genuinely hairline, low-contrast treatment would have to earn its thumbnail legibility from the geometry instead, and that is the harder problem this work has not yet solved.
marketResponse: PASS — visible at browse size and it is the claimed change. I described it blind before reading the brief: stress contracts the figure toward the center and thins the satellites; recovery expands past neutral to the largest, brightest, most populated state. 9190 goes from roughly 240px of reach at neutral to about 170 at stress and past 250 at recovery, with satellites pulled in and then flung out and elongated; 9369 runs about 155 to 110 to 180; 9548 contracts and swaps its orbiting squares for four open circles, then returns packed. This matches 'it opens out in recovery and draws in under stress', and it is carried by geometry — element count, reach and member kind — rather than by line weight, which is what the brief required. One weak case: 9011's outer hexagon barely contracts under stress; it drops a ring member and swells its interior instead, so its reach reads almost unchanged.
tokenIdentity: PASS — each of the four tokens on the states sheet stays recognisably itself across all three rows. Base polygon, palette, symmetry order and satellite family persist; 9011 is the same nested hexagon, 9190 the same six-satellite hex, 9369 the same three-dotted circle, 9548 the same star-lattice disc. The only wobble is 9548's satellites changing kind from squares to circles under stress, which is a noticeable but not identity-breaking substitution.
composition: Mostly sound, one bad token. Focal hierarchy is clear and consistent — bright rim, mid slate rings, small central cluster — and the centered emblem sits in generous margin at roughly 60-75% of frame. Nothing is mushy at 256 and there is no filled mass anywhere. The failure is 10980: satellite hexagons are hard-sliced by the canvas at top-left and bottom-right and there are four disconnected line fragments floating at the top, bottom, left and right edges, which read as escaped members clipped by the frame rather than as a composed bleed. 10264 has a similar stray dash. If threads are meant to extend past the frame that needs to be a deliberate, repeated gesture; here it looks like overflow.
reasoning: Five of the brief's six clauses land, and several land well — the palette is exact, the radial figure is exact, the market transformation is real, geometry-carried and visible at browse size, and the twelve are genuinely twelve. But the clause that fails is the one the brief is named after and repeats four times, and it fails on the majority of tokens. The proof is my own stage-1 description, written blind: I reached for seal, sigil, schematic, carrier line and heavy alpha layering, and never once for delicate, fine, fragile, thread or provisional. The brief anticipated this exact outcome in its own words — keep the contrast low 'so the lines read as thread rather than as structure' — and a cold reader read structure. The measurements confirm it rather than merely flavour it: a near-white 217-luminance stroke on a 15-luminance ground at 5-6px on a 256px canvas is a bold confident rim, not hairline, and it is the single loudest element in eight of the twelve. This is competent, coherent, well-composed work; it is not the fragile thing that was asked for, and briefFidelity is a gate that no amount of quality elsewhere can buy past. Refusing here is also cheap: the gap is a stroke-weight and luminance parameter, not a redesign, and this is the last moment before a permanent on-chain commitment.
wouldChange: Take the bone carrier stroke down to a true hairline and pull its luminance off near-white — target roughly 3-5:1 line-to-ground contrast instead of the current ~13:1, with the stroke nearer 1-2px at 256 rather than 5-6 — and let the pale slate mid-tones carry more of the figure so no single member dominates as a rim. The collection must then re-earn its 120px legibility from geometry, symmetry order and reach rather than from one bright outline; 9906, 9011 and 10622 are the tokens to test it on, since they are the furthest from filigree today. Fix 10980's edge clipping in the same pass.
